dedupe_keys.name: nlr festiv flexible energy scheduling tool for integrating variable generation multi timescale unit commitment dispatch and agc simulation

description: FESTIV is a National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) power system operations model that simulates how variability and uncertainty from variable generation affect operations. Contents: a multiple-timescale simulation that chains security-constrained unit commitment, security-constrained economic dispatch and automatic generation control sub-models, each feeding the next, and so mimics operator behaviour; it is fully configurable to test operating temporal resolutions and operating reserve strategies (regulating, following, contingency and ramping reserves) and reports both economic and reliability metrics. Producer: NLR Grid Modernization; described in the paper 'A Flexible Power System Operations Simulation Model for Assessing Wind Integration' and related NLR reports from 2011 to 2014. Coverage: generic power systems configured by the user. Format and access: documentation and papers on the NLR page; the page does not give a model download. Licence: not stated on the NLR page. Caveats: the page points users to NLR's newer Sienna tools as the up-to-date suite for studying variability and uncertainty, so FESTIV is a legacy model. Simulation uses: studying reserve requirements, scheduling resolution and balancing performance with high wind and solar shares, and reliability and cost trade-offs in operations. Related records: platform-sienna, platform-helics and data-rts-gmlc.
